criteria.check: Every reported number (metric, count, percentage, p-value) can be traced to a result file, table or tool output in the evidence. A number that appears only in the answer is a violation.
A claim that a method beats a baseline compares both under the same data split, budget and metric, and says so. A comparison with mismatched setups, or one whose setup is not stated, is a violation.
The answer states what was not verified or not run (for example missing seeds, untested datasets, unchecked citations) instead of implying full coverage.
Each significance claim names the test used, the sample size and whether it is one- or two-sided.
Each significance claim reports an effect size or confidence interval, not only a p-value.
When several hypotheses are tested together, the answer says whether and how it corrected for multiple comparisons.
